cases.evidence_boundary: Use only claims and citations verified from the retrieved primary-paper links; do not infer comparative results.
cases.request: Write one compact Related Work paragraph that positions an action-conditioned latent world model.
facts: The proposed method predicts latent transitions conditioned on actions.
It is evaluated for planning, not for open-loop video generation.
Use only citations that the writer verifies from the supplied source links.
manual_rubric: Organize prior work by technical axes rather than as a paper list.
Distinguish planning models from open-loop visual prediction.
Verify every literature claim in the primary papers before adding citations.

machine_checks.message: Use the field-standard latent-transition or latent-dynamics term.
Preserve planning as the evaluated use.
Do not add an unsupported ranking claim.

cases.evidence_boundary: Answer only from Table 4; no significance test or additional experiment exists.
cases.request: Answer a reviewer who asks whether the gains are robust across random seeds.
facts: Table 4 reports five seeds.
The mean improvement is 3.2 points.
No statistical significance test was run.
No additional experiment may be claimed.
manual_rubric: Lead with a direct answer to the robustness question.
Separate the observed multi-seed mean from an untested significance claim.
Do not over-concede beyond the evidence boundary.

machine_checks.message: State that significance was not tested.
Do not invent an additional experiment.

cases.evidence_boundary: Translate the proposition exactly; preserve modality, negative significance, and the unverified generalization boundary.
cases.request: Translate: 该方法在5个随机种子中的3个上有所提升，可能缓解模型误差累积，但差异不具有统计显著性；其对未见过的机器人形态的泛化能力仍有待验证。
manual_rubric: Preserve three of five seeds and possibility rather than causality.
Preserve the lack of statistical significance.
Do not claim demonstrated generalization to unseen embodiments.

machine_checks.message: Preserve three of five random seeds.
Use a standard model-error accumulation term.

cases.evidence_boundary: Describe only the declared observation, prediction, execution, and replanning interface.
cases.request: Define the action interface of a language-conditioned robot policy without implying that chunk prediction is fully open-loop.
facts: The policy predicts 16 future actions.
It executes four actions before observing again and replanning.
The language instruction and two camera views condition every policy query.
manual_rubric: Distinguish prediction horizon from execution horizon.
Describe the controller as closed-loop at the replanning interval.
Name every conditioning input without inventing architecture details.

machine_checks.message: State the feedback or replanning boundary.
Name language and two camera views.
Do not describe the full predicted chunk as open-loop execution.

cases.evidence_boundary: Report only the supplied tasks, trials, success criterion, data budget, aggregation, and interval.
cases.request: Write a reproducible experimental-setup paragraph for the real-robot evaluation.
facts: There are six tasks and 20 trials per task.
A trial succeeds only if the object reaches the target region without human intervention.
All methods use the same 120 demonstrations per task.
Results report mean task success and a Wilson 95% confidence interval over trials.
manual_rubric: Make the trial denominator and exact success event reproducible.
State the matched demonstration budget as a comparison control.
Do not invent hardware, control frequency, seeds, or baseline versions.

machine_checks.pattern: (?:six|6)(?: [a-z-]+){0,3} tasks?[\s\S]{0,80}(?:20|twenty) trials? per task|(?:20|twenty) trials? per task[\s\S]{0,80}(?:six|6)(?: [a-z-]+){0,3} tasks?
machine_checks.message: State six tasks and 20 trials per task.

machine_checks.pattern: target region.*without human intervention|without human intervention.*target region
machine_checks.message: State the exact binary success event.

machine_checks.pattern: (?:same|matched)[\s\S]{0,40}120 demonstrations? (?:per|for each) task|120 demonstrations? (?:per|for each) task[\s\S]{0,40}(?:same|matched)

cases.evidence_boundary: Analyze the matched measurements only; the study does not identify a causal component.
cases.request: Analyze the main result without hiding the quality–latency trade-off.
facts: Success increases from 62% to 70%.
Inference latency increases from 40 ms to 68 ms on the same hardware.
The gain occurs on four of six tasks; two tasks are unchanged within uncertainty.
The study does not identify which component causes the gain.
manual_rubric: Interpret evidence only after reporting both endpoints and the matched condition.
Retain the two unchanged tasks rather than reporting only the aggregate gain.
Do not attribute the gain to an unisolated component.

machine_checks.message: Do not invent a causal component attribution.

cases.evidence_boundary: Limit motivation and contributions to the proposed planner and the three offline-control benchmarks.
cases.request: Draft the limitation-to-design bridge and contribution paragraph for an offline world-model paper.
facts: Prior methods assume dense action coverage in the offline dataset.
The proposed uncertainty-aware planner avoids trajectories far from dataset support.
Experiments evaluate return and support violation rate on three offline-control benchmarks.
No real-robot or online-adaptation experiment was conducted.
manual_rubric: Connect the dense-coverage assumption causally to the design choice without overstating proof.
Pair empirical contributions with return and support-violation evidence.
Keep deployment and adaptation outside the claimed contribution.

machine_checks.message: State how the planner treats unsupported trajectories.
Do not claim untested deployment or online adaptation.

cases.evidence_boundary: The abstract may claim only unseen-object generalization in simulation over four benchmarks and five seeds.
cases.request: Draft a compact abstract from the completed paper facts.
facts: The method improves success from 48% to 57% on unseen-object manipulation.
The difference is nine percentage points over four benchmarks.
Evaluation is simulation-only and uses five seeds.
No evidence supports unseen-embodiment transfer.
manual_rubric: Keep problem, method, evidence, and scope in a compact abstract arc.
Name unseen objects as the tested generalization axis.
Do not imply unseen-embodiment transfer.

machine_checks.message: Do not invent a state-of-the-art claim.

cases.evidence_boundary: Separate observed long-horizon degradation from untested real-robot behavior; do not generalize beyond horizon 50.
cases.request: Write a limitations paragraph that distinguishes an observed world-model failure from an untested deployment setting.
facts: Planning performance degrades beyond an imagination horizon of 50 steps.
Prediction error increases with rollout length, but the study does not establish a causal threshold.
Evaluation uses simulated locomotion only.
Real-robot robustness was not evaluated.
manual_rubric: State the observed failure before proposing an explanation.
Do not turn the horizon observation into a universal causal threshold.
Distinguish simulated evidence from untested real-robot robustness.

machine_checks.message: State that real-robot robustness is untested.
Do not invent a universal causal threshold.

cases.evidence_boundary: Conclude from the three reported offline tasks and three seeds only; online and robot deployment are untested.
cases.request: Write a concise conclusion that restates the contribution and result without broadening the empirical scope.
facts: A conservative value penalty is added to an offline actor-critic method.
Normalized return increases from 71 to 76 across three D4RL tasks.
Results average three seeds.
Online fine-tuning and robot deployment were not evaluated.
manual_rubric: Synthesize contribution and evidence rather than repeating the abstract verbatim.
Preserve the dataset, task, and seed scope.
End with a bounded future direction rather than an unsupported capability claim.

machine_checks.message: Do not claim untested online or robot deployment.

cases.evidence_boundary: The caption must define the timing boundary and measurement protocol; it may not imply hardware-independent ranking.
cases.request: Write a self-contained caption for an efficiency table comparing throughput and end-to-end latency.
facts: The reported method reaches 43 images/s and 21 ms end-to-end latency.
Measurements use one NVIDIA A100, batch size 1, and FP16 inference.
Timing excludes model loading and includes preprocessing and action decoding.
Each value follows 100 warm-up iterations and 1,000 measured iterations.
manual_rubric: Make the caption understandable without consulting the body text.
Define metric units, hardware, batch, precision, timing boundary, and repetitions.
Do not rank results measured under incomparable hardware or timing boundaries.

machine_checks.pattern: 43 (?:images/s|images per second).*(?:21 ms)|21 ms.*43 (?:images/s|images per second)
machine_checks.message: Report throughput and latency with units.
Do not imply a hardware-independent ranking.

cases.evidence_boundary: The table supports held-out-kitchen evaluation only; it does not establish cross-embodiment or open-world generalization.
cases.request: Write a self-contained caption for a VLA generalization table with explicit train/test axes and trial denominators.
facts: Policies train in four kitchens and are evaluated in two held-out kitchens.
The table covers eight language-conditioned manipulation tasks.
Each method uses the same checkpoint and 25 trials per task in each held-out kitchen.
Cells report binary task success rate; higher is better.
manual_rubric: Make the training and held-out environment axis explicit.
State task count, trial denominator, checkpoint control, metric, and direction.
Do not convert held-out-kitchen evidence into cross-embodiment or open-world generalization.

machine_checks.pattern: (?:four|4) kitchens?.*(?:two|2) held[- ]out kitchens?|(?:two|2) held[- ]out kitchens?.*(?:four|4) kitchens?
machine_checks.message: State the train and held-out kitchen counts.

machine_checks.pattern: (?:binary )?task success rate.*higher is better|higher is better.*(?:binary )?task success rate

machine_checks.message: Do not broaden the tested generalization axis.
